name: Gray Goshawk
rangeDescription: Northern and eastern australia including tasmania
description: Heavily built and powerful forest raptor occurring in two color morphs: all white; or gray and white. Both morphs have yellow legs, red eyes.

name: Tawny-chested Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Eastern nicaragua to northern costa rica (southward to puerto limón)
description: Fairly small flycatcher with limited range on the Caribbean slope from Nicaragua to Costa Rica. Rather distinctive with combination of gray head, warm tawny breast, olive back, and tawny wingbars.

name: White-bellied Cinclodes
rangeDescription: Andes of central peru (junín, lima, and huancavelica)
description: Striking, critically endangered bird found only at extremely high elevations in the Andes of central Peru. One of the most beautiful members of the ovenbird family, with immaculate white underparts and wing patches contrasting with its deep chestnut upperparts and gray crown.

name: Bay-vented Cotinga
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of central peru
description: Uncommon cotinga found only in very high-elevation forest near treeline in the eastern Andes of central Peru. Adult plumage is gray with a tan breast and belly and a chestnut vent.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Slate-colored Antbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to northeastern ecuador, eastern peru, and west-central amazonian brazil
description: Medium-sized antbird. Males are gray with small white spots on the wings, and females are cinnamon with pale spots on the wings.

name: Yellow-breasted Tailorbird
rangeDescription: East-central philippines (bohol, leyte, and samar)
description: A small, long-billed, long-tailed bird of dense undergrowth in lowland forest on Bohol, Leyte, and Samar islands. Olive-green on the back and wings, with an orange-brown tail often held cocked, yellow underparts, a thin yellow line around the back of the neck, and a black cap.

name: Yellow-eared Parrot
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia and northern ecuador
description: Endangered macaw-like parrot found in Andean cloud forest. Likely only occurs in Colombia now, but formerly ranged as far south as central Ecuador.

name: White-gaped Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Northern australia (king sound, western australia to townsville, queensland)
description: A medium to large honeyeater with a sooty brown plumage and a bright pale patch between its eye and bill. Much larger than the similarly colored Dusky Honeyeater.

name: Lowland Peltops
rangeDescription: Lowlands of new guinea, including waigeo, salawati, and misool (raja ampat islands, off western new guinea)
description: A medium-sized bird of lowland forest edge and clearings. Distinctive plumage.

name: Okarito Brown Kiwi
rangeDescription: Okarito forest (west coast of south island, new zealand)
description: A large, dark grayish brown kiwi with brownish streaking, often showing white patches on face. Restricted to native forest near Okarito in New Zealand, with small populations on predator-free Mana, Blumine, and Motuara islands.

name: Palau Fantail
rangeDescription: Palau (babelthuap to peleliu)
description: Small, with a long, often fanned tail. Mostly pale orange-red with a gleaming white throat and a black chest with gray sides.

name: Wied's Tyrant-Manakin
rangeDescription: Coastal southeastern brazil (southern bahia, espírito santo, and minas gerais)
description: Nondescript manakin that may be mistaken for a flycatcher. Has an olive-green back, a grayish throat, and yellowish underparts.

name: Least Storm-Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds islands off baja california; ranges southward to far northern peru
description: Very small, all-dark storm-petrel with a fairly short, graduated tail. Fairly common and can be seen from shore in the Gulf of California and along the Pacific coast.

name: Black-breasted Kite
rangeDescription: Northern and interior plains and scrub of australia
description: A large dark raptor. In flight it shows a very short stubby tail, and has large pale wing panels.

name: Hudsonian Godwit
rangeDescription: Breeds locally in alaska and northern canada (east to hudson bay); winters in southern south america (argentina and south-central chile), southward to tierra del fuego
description: The smallest godwit, overall rather dark. Long upturned bill, red at the base with a black tip.

name: Cinnamon-vented Piha
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (espírito santo and minas gerais to northeastern santa catarina)
description: A quite large thrushlike bird with a robust beak. Grayish and slightly scaling-looking on the head and back with browner wings and tail, and gray-brown underparts.

name: Apurimac Spinetail
rangeDescription: Andes of southern peru (bosque de ampay region of apurímac)
description: Small, long-tailed bird found locally in humid montane forest in the Apurimac valley. Dark slaty gray with a rusty red cap and wings.

name: Melanesian Megapode
rangeDescription: Admiralty islands, new ireland, and new britain (bismarck archipelago), and solomon islands
description: A large-bodied, small-headed bird of odd proportions. Plumage is mostly dark, with dark legs and a dark head, but in good light shows a yellowish bill and reddish bare skin on the forehead with a very short light gray crest.

name: Juba Weaver
rangeDescription: Riparian vegetation of southeastern ethiopia, juba region of southern somalia, and northeastern kenya
description: A fairly small, compact weaver with a large bill. Breeding males are colorful, with a black head, a red eye, a rufous chest, and a yellow belly and back.

name: Kilimanjaro White-eye
rangeDescription: Northern tanzania (mount kilimanjaro, mount meru, and arusha regions)
description: A small, sharp-billed warbler-like bird, olive-yellow with very broad white spectacles around the eyes. Found in montane forest, forest edge, and lush gardens and scrub, usually in hyperactive flocks.
